flags.title: NC Medicaid Expanded December 2023 — Infrastructure Still Maturing
flags.summary: ~600,000 previously uninsured adults became eligible. NC Medicaid Direct (managed care) still maturing. Plans: WellCare, AmeriHealth Caritas, Blue Cross NC, Carolina Complete Health, UHC Community Plan. Screen every adult 19-64 without insurance for NC Medicaid eligibility FIRST. Apply: ePass.nc.gov.

flags.title: Farmworker Community — Largest in Southeast, Specialized Legal Services Required
flags.summary: Hundreds of thousands of H-2A visa workers and undocumented workers in tobacco, sweet potato, hog, poultry, cucumber. Geographic: coastal plain (Duplin, Sampson, Wayne, Johnston). Issues: wage theft, housing conditions, workers comp, OSHA, immigration. DO NOT use standard legal aid. Route: Legal Aid NC Farmworker Unit (919-856-2180), NC Justice Center (919-856-2570), NC Farmworker Health (919-857-4330).

flags.title: NC UI — $350/Week Max, 12-20 Weeks, 10-DAY Appeal — Second Shortest in Registry
flags.summary: Max $350/week (very low for state of its size). Duration: 12-20 weeks (sliding scale). Appeal deadline: 10 DAYS from mailing — second shortest in registry. Contact legal aid within 5 days of any denial. NC DES: des.nc.gov / 888-737-0259.

flags.title: NC SNAP ABAWD — Active, Limited Waivers
flags.summary: SNAP ABAWD work requirements active for most counties. Some rural counties with high unemployment may qualify for exemptions — check current NC DHHS waiver list. Critical exemptions: disability, caregiving, pregnancy, education. Apply: ePass.nc.gov or local county DSS.

flags.title: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians — Major Sovereignty Infrastructure in Western NC
flags.summary: Qualla Boundary (56,000+ acres in Great Smoky Mountains). ~14,000 enrolled members. Harrah's Cherokee Casino revenue. Services: Tribal TANF, housing, health, education, elder. ICWA mandatory for child welfare. EBCI Social Services: 828-497-7000. Cherokee Indian Hospital: 828-497-9163. Distinct from Cherokee Nation of Oklahoma.

flags.title: NC Civil Rights — NCHRC 180-Day SOL, No State LGBTQ+ Protection
flags.summary: NC does NOT have state civil rights law protecting sexual orientation or gender identity. All LGBTQ+ claims must route through federal EEOC only. HB2 controversy (2016) — partially repealed but political climate means state enforcement limited. Always dual-file EEOC AND NCHRC. HUD primary for housing discrimination.

flags.title: Charlotte Metro — Rapid Growth, Diverse Communities, Housing Cost Crisis
flags.summary: Largest city in NC, major banking/finance hub. Latino 16%+, large Black community, growing immigrant population. Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy: 704-376-1600. Mecklenburg County DSS: 704-336-3000. Atrium Health charity care: 704-355-2000. Housing market rapid rent increases — at intake, housing cost burden typically the presenting crisis.

flags.title: NC Wage Claim — State Process Weak, Federal WHD Primary
flags.summary: NCWHA mirrors FLSA but limited enforcement capacity. NC DOL wage process slower/less resourced than federal WHD. For most claims: file federal WHD as primary (Raleigh: 919-790-2741, Charlotte: 704-749-3360). Farmworker wage claims: route to Legal Aid NC Farmworker Unit, NOT general wage process. NCWHA private lawsuit: 2-year SOL.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: North Carolina Involuntary Commitment
flags.message: NC involuntary psychiatric hold law: North Carolina Involuntary Commitment. Statutory authority: N.C.G.S. § 122C-261. Maximum initial hold duration: 24 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 24 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in NC retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in NC: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: North Carolina Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: North Carolina Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
